correctness.rationale: The squared radial function is strictly decreasing with circular distance to the nearest axis for every 0<p<2. On a period L=π/2 and for 0<d≤L/2, the two profiles cross at d/2 and (L+d)/2. Between these points the first is the minimum; reflection t↦d−t modulo L interchanges the profiles and the two complementary half-periods. Integrating therefore gives I=4∫[d/2,(L+d)/2] fₚ(t)dt, also at d=0 by continuity. This yields the exact formula and strictly negative interior derivative. At the minimum the centered sum is even analytic with quadratic coefficient −fₚ′(π/8)>0. Near the axis fₚ(t)=1−(2/p)tᵖ+O(t^{2p}+t²), and near the diagonal the first change is O(t²); integrating yields the displayed coefficient and little-o remainder for all fixed 0<p<2. The astroid substitution gives 3u²/(1+u²)³ and differentiation verifies its primitive; independent quadrature gives minimum 0.845064236407053630. At p=1 the first nonlinear term is the integer power d² (analytic on the folded branch); the signed-angle profile still has a linear absolute-value cusp. The formulas need no repair; the fractional/nonanalytic description of the nonlinear term is understood only for p≠1.
